title: Macondo / Deepwater Horizon: blowout, safety-critical elements, and offshore process-safety regime gaps
summary: Macondo is encoded as an offshore process-safety and barrier-management record: temporary-abandonment work, loss of well control, blowout-preventer failure, safety-critical-element management, contractor/regulator interfaces, and leading-indicator gaps are the first-pass grain.

status_history.note: Added as process-safety / CSB lane record.

place.location: Macondo well / Deepwater Horizon drilling rig, Gulf of Mexico, United States

subjects.name: Deepwater Horizon drilling rig and Macondo well
U.S. Chemical Safety and Hazard Investigation Board

claims.claim: The CSB Macondo overview says that on April 20, 2010, control of the Macondo well was lost during temporary abandonment, causing a blowout; hydrocarbons ignited on the rig, explosions and fire killed 11 people, seriously injured 17, sank the rig, and caused massive marine/coastal damage from a reported about 5 million barrels of released hydrocarbons.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: The CSB overview frames the investigation from a process-safety perspective, including hierarchy of controls, human factors, inherent safety, corporate culture/decision-making, management of organizational change, contractor oversight, shared responsibilities, and similarities to past CSB investigations including BP Texas City.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: The CSB release states that the blowout preventer intended to shut off high-pressure oil and gas failed to seal the well because drill pipe buckled for reasons the offshore drilling industry remained largely unaware of; the report called for better management of safety-critical elements.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: The CSB overview says its Macondo investigation emphasized safety-critical elements, design/testing limitations that might otherwise remain undetected, regulatory treatment of such equipment, human factors, and leading process-safety indicators for active monitoring of safety-critical equipment and systems.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: For the cube, Macondo is a process-safety barrier record for offshore systems: final barriers, safety-critical elements, contractor/regulator interfaces, and leading indicator regimes matter before the blowout, not only during emergency response.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

type_payload.incident_class: offshore blowout, explosion, fire, environmental disaster
type_payload.system: well control system, blowout preventer, temporary-abandonment procedures, contractor/operator/regulator process-safety regime

sequence_of_events.event: Temporary-abandonment activities occurred at the Macondo well.
Well control was lost, hydrocarbons released forcefully to rig level, and an ignition source caused explosions and fire.
The rig sank and prolonged hydrocarbon release caused major marine/coastal damage.
CSB examined the case as process safety, including safety-critical elements, human factors, MOC, contractor oversight, and regulatory regimes.

type_payload.proximate_cause: Loss of well control and blowout followed by ignition; BOP failed to seal during emergency well-control efforts.
latent_conditions: offshore major-accident hazard management less aligned with mature process-safety concepts than other high-hazard sectors
final barrier treated as reliable without enough independent evidence of performance under buckled-pipe conditions

handling_notes: Preserve worker/community dignity and avoid casualty spectacle.
Use investigation language to understand system conditions, not to assign unsourced individual blame.
Record source boundaries and avoid regulatory/political overreach.
